A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same stochastic-integral framework for discrete diffusion models. Their main text, equations, algorithms, Figure 1, and Appendices A–C are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Figure 1 on page 6 presents original example stochastic trajectories under two specified evolving Poisson intensities. These constitute illustrative simulation outcomes, although the paper otherwise concentrates on theory.

after.justification: Figure 1 on page 5 retains the illustrative simulation with different sample trajectories. The main text and appendices otherwise report mathematical analysis rather than benchmark experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the printed update by adding the current state to the jump sum and evaluating each Poisson mean at the appropriate time and destination. This aligns the pseudocode with the integral formulation and proof already in v1; the underlying samplers and training objective are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same illustrative nearest-neighbor jump process under two evolving intensity profiles in Figure 1. No datasets, application tasks, or additional simulation scenarios are introduced.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical baseline comparisons. The comparisons involving τ-leaping, uniformization, and earlier papers remain theoretical, with the same algorithms considered.

E3.justification: Figure 1 retains its time range and stated intensity rule, λt(y) = 50ft for neighboring states and zero otherwise. No evaluation metrics, sample counts, or experimental procedures are revised; changed theorem parameters belong to the theoretical analysis.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or additional empirical case-study questions are added. Figure 1 continues to illustrate the same relationship between intensity and jump frequency; the new multiple-jump analysis is a mathematical proof.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies seeds, repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests for Figure 1. The new high-probability theorem qualification is a theoretical guarantee, not a change in empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 1 contains different realized jump times and state sequences in v2 under the retained intensity profiles. Its qualitative message remains unchanged, and the replacement trajectories do not demonstrate a performance improvement.

T1.justification: V2 adds Proposition A.14 and its multiple-jump probability argument, and qualifies Theorem 4.7 with probability 1 - O(epsilon). Theorem C.6 now concerns the alternative interpolation (A.15) and replaces an equality with an upper bound. Theorem 2.1 also revises the epsilon dependence of the step size and the logarithmic dependence of the step count. These materially revise the central analysis.

C1.justification: The introduction drops regularity from its explicit list of assumptions claimed to be relaxed. The principal contributions remain the unified stochastic-integral framework, the first claimed KL bound for τ-leaping, and the theoretical comparison with uniformization; the abstract is unchanged.

C2.justification: New Remark A.13 acknowledges the additive structure implicitly required by τ-leaping, possible state-space boundary violations, and their connection to multiple jumps. This adds a substantive applicability qualification absent from v1, while the existing early-stopping and dimensional-complexity interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Remark A.13 newly describes clipping to handle boundary violations on ordered spaces such as [S]^d. This supplies implementation guidance for the existing algorithm without establishing that a revised implementation was evaluated.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including Hyvärinen and Dayan (2005), Ren et al. (2025), and several parallel-sampling papers. The introduction also characterizes earlier discrete analyses as algorithm-specific. The principal research positioning remains unchanged; the Poisson-measure literature discussion is largely relocated to Appendix A.

P1.justification: V2 adds intuitive explanations in Sections 3–4 and a proof roadmap in Appendix C.1, and moves existing background and martingale remarks into Appendix A. Local prose, affiliations, and publication headers are edited, while the overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with replacement trajectories and relocated from page 6 to page 5, retaining its axes and caption. Algorithm 1 and several equations are reformatted, with corresponding text and page reflow.

improvement.justification: V2 improves consistency and transparency by correcting the printed τ-leaping update, explaining previously implicit boundary requirements, and adding a proof roadmap. The new appendix argument accompanies a weaker, high-probability qualification of Theorem 4.7, rather than a stronger convergence guarantee. The clearest net gains are therefore limited improvements in documentation and clarity about the analysis.
